newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq, Jordan to increase trade in 1997, press.
newsitem.headline: Iraq, Jordan to increase trade in 1997, press.

text.p: Iraq and Jordan have agreed to increase trade by $35 million to reach $255 million for 1997, Iraqi newspapers reported on Sunday.
The papers said Iraq would pay $50 million to Jordan for debts accumulated from previous trade accords. The amount would be paid by Iraqi oil exports to Jordan.
Jordanian oil imports from Iraq in 1997 will increase by seven percent over last year, the newspapers said.

They said Iraq and Jordan reached agreement on Saturday at the end of a visit paid by Jordan's trade and industry mininster, Ali Abu al-Ragheb, and the minister for energy and mineral resources, Hashem Dabbas.
The accord was signed by the ministers with Iraq's trade minister, Mohammed Mehdi Saleh and oil minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed.

"The two sides have agreed to increase the volume of trade stated by the bilateral cooperation protocol from last year's $220 million to $255 million this year in order to bring to Iraq more food and medicine," said al-Thawra, newspaper of the ruling Baath party.
Iraq pays for its imports from Jordan by exporting crude oil and oil products which are exempt from U.N. trade sanctions slapped on Baghdad in 1990 for its invasion of Kuwait.

Out of the 75,000 barrels per day exported at present, Jordan paid market prices for 25,000 bpd of crude and for another 25,000 bpd of by-products. The rest is traded at undisclosed concessionary terms.
"The minutes of the Iraqi-Jordanian commission for economic cooperation...include an increase of oil exports to Jordan by seven percent over figures of last year," said al-Thawra.
